leads.name: Conqueror's Oak (King's Oak), Windsor Great Park
leads.reason: No current girth or fix seen on a fetched page. Wikipedia places it in Cranbourne Park; old texts give conflicting girth (26 ft at 3 ft; 38 ft) and age 1,000 to 1,200 years. Needs a second source, a coordinate and an access check (Cranbourne Gate side is open, but King Offa's Oak nearby is in a private area).

leads.name: Signing Oak, Windsor Great Park
leads.reason: Queen's Green Canopy '70 Ancient Trees' page says 900 years old, Windsor Great Park. No girth, no location, no access statement. Needs a second source and a position. A search snippet of a Sketchfab model page gives about 1,000 years and 9.94 m girth with hollow trunk (not a source).

leads.name: Old pollard oak at Forest Gate, Windsor Great Park
leads.reason: Only a search snippet of a British Library album catalogue (19th-century, 26 ft 10 in at 5 ft, probable age 800 years); not a fetched page, and no evidence it still stands. Needs a modern source and a position.

leads.name: Pollard oak on Smith's Lawn, Windsor Great Park
leads.reason: Same British Library snippet (31 ft 9 in at 5 ft, probable age 800 years), not fetched, 19th-century, no position; Smith's Lawn is a Guards Polo area, access not checked.

leads.held_why: Held twice by writing passes (2026-11-10, 2026-11-11): three trees up to a kilometre apart in one lead, not one collectible point; Tree Register only, measured 2008, no check they stand; no Windsor place file exists. Split into three leads with a dated sighting each before writing.
